subject: Would appreciate someone checking my diagram - trying to do cross-sectional mixed effects model

messages.author: c1d90967b611a5b6
messages.subject: Would appreciate someone checking my diagram - trying to do cross-sectional mixed effects model
parts:
Some background: we asked a series of questions to gay men in a relationship and want to see what the relationship of a certain Attribute is on their Behavior (both LVs, measured through a series of Likert items). We would also like to adjust for some other variables that may influence the Behavior.

We might expect the people in a relationship to be more similar compared to others in the sample, so we're adding a random intercept to account for this clustering. Also, since the relationship is "symmetric", i.e. there's no marked role differences as there might be in a heterosexual relationship, I would expect that the loadings and path coefficients should be equal for both people in the relationship.

Given those restrictions, here's a mockup of what the model would look like (we actually have >8 items per LV, just showing 3 for simplicity):

























I'm just a statistician and this is my first time using SEM so I would be very grateful if more experienced users can give their opinions on whether this model makes sense.

messages.subject: Re: Would appreciate someone checking my diagram - trying to do cross-sectional mixed effects model
parts: I would be very grateful if more experienced users can give their opinions on whether this model makes sense.

Makes sense to me.  I would also add the Attribute covariance, which should be an estimated model parameter (or you could replace the covariance with another random intercept, like you did for the Behaviors, which fits more conceptually with a multilevel modeling approach -- but latent variables are latent variables, whether we call them common factors, person parameters, or random effects).
